objectives.statement: Connect two activities actually attempted using specific evidence.
Explain a justified revision or uncertainty without inventing completed work.
Ask a useful next question and say how evidence could help answer it.

scenes.title: Read a reflection with a reason

content.body: This short reflection is fictional. It shows how a learner uses evidence, not just confidence. Your reflection should describe your own work.

accessibility.textAlternative: This short reflection is fictional. It shows how a learner uses evidence, not just confidence. Your reflection should describe your own work. An illustrative reflection. I first added when the score instruction said set. I checked my trace against the instruction. Set replaced the previous score, so I revised that step. It reminded me to match each site claim to the right observation in Social Studies. Tomorrow I want to test another event order.

offline.fallback: Use the printed text, diagrams and questions with paper and pencil. Responses can be spoken and scribed.

glossary.meaning: An explanation of learning, evidence and a next question.

content.body: A useful reflection points to a real detail and explains its meaning. A changed idea is not a failure. Sometimes the evidence supports keeping an idea, or leaves a question open.

prompts.prompt: Explain how one detail supports a change in thinking.

accessibility.textAlternative: A useful reflection points to a real detail and explains its meaning. A changed idea is not a failure. Sometimes the evidence supports keeping an idea, or leaves a question open. What supports the pupil's revision? Options: Greater confidence is enough to establish the answer without checking.; The set instruction and the trace show which step needed changing.; Feeling certain proves the original step was right.. What should a learner do with a valid result that challenges an idea? Options: Hide it so the original idea still appears correct.; Remove the conflicting result before sharing the reflection.; Keep it and explain what it changes or leaves uncertain.. Explain how one detail supports a change in thinking.

offline.fallback: Use the printed text, diagrams and questions with paper and pencil. Responses can be spoken and scribed.

options.text: Greater confidence is enough to establish the answer without checking.
options.feedback: Confidence does not identify what the trace showed.

options.text: The set instruction and the trace show which step needed changing.
options.feedback: This response explains the relevant evidence and what it supports.

options.text: Feeling certain proves the original step was right.
options.feedback: Feeling certain cannot replace checking the instruction.

items.prompt: What should a learner do with a valid result that challenges an idea?

options.text: Hide it so the original idea still appears correct.
options.feedback: Hiding evidence prevents an honest explanation of the revision.

options.text: Remove the conflicting result before sharing the reflection.
options.feedback: The conflicting result is useful evidence; explain it rather than removing it.

options.text: Keep it and explain what it changes or leaves uncertain.
options.feedback: This response explains the relevant evidence and what it supports.

scenes.title: Reflect on work you actually attempted

content.body: Choose two activities you actually tried today. Use a sentence, calculation, trace, sketch or recorded observation. Label counted observations, given information, worked-out calculations and your conclusion honestly. Unfinished work may be discussed as unfinished.

prompts.prompt: Name the two tasks and a specific piece of evidence. Explain one similarity and one difference in the reasoning.
Explain a revision, a supported original idea or an uncertainty. Distinguish given information from your own observation.

scenes.title: Make the reflection useful for tomorrow

content.body: Read your reflection or have it read aloud. Replace a vague statement with a specific reason. End with one question you could investigate. You do not need to claim that every task was completed or that every question is solved.

prompts.prompt: Show the sentence you improved and explain why it is clearer.
Ask one question for tomorrow and describe what evidence could help answer it.
